source.title: Beyond the Last Layer: Multi-Layer Representation Fusion for Visual Tokenization
source.authors: Xuan-Yu Zhu; Yan Bai; Yang Shi; Yihang Lou; Yuan-Xing Zhang; Jing-Yi Jin; Yuan Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and table formatting are flattened, but the scaling results and their values are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests an analogous scaling relationship in image tokenizers, a new modality: fusion-module capacity and fused-layer count are varied, and image reconstruction quality is measured. It does not test language-model pretraining loss or compute-optimal language-model allocation.
record.gate_note: The scaling experiments test visual-tokenizer reconstruction quality (rFID) against fusion-module capacity and fused-layer count. Other reconstruction, generation, text-to-image, and ablation results are reported, but do not test the claim versions about language-model scaling or demonstrate downstream performance scaling. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper scales only a small trainable fusion adapter (2.5M–113M parameters) inside a frozen DINOv2-B encoder and frozen decoder. It measures ImageNet reconstruction rFID, not held-out training loss, and fits a log-linear relation, not a power law. The range is about 1.6 orders of magnitude, and the analogy drawn is to NLP vocabulary scaling. Varying adapter capacity in a frozen pipeline, judged by a perceptual metric, is a related but different construct from model, data or compute scaling of loss. The finding goes under fits_no_version rather than as a V5 test. Kaplan and Hoffmann are not cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also present DRoRAE as improving rFID 0.57→0.29 and gFID (with AutoGuidance) 1.74→1.65, with comparable text-to-image GenEval. They claim both capacity and layer-count axes follow one log-linear trend against trainable parameters, framed as analogous to vocabulary scaling in NLP, not to model-size scaling laws. Future work: larger encoders and video tokenization.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales fusion-module capacity and fused-layer count for an image tokenizer and measures reconstruction rFID, rather than scaling language-model parameters, training tokens, or compute and measuring held-out cross-entropy loss.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationship varies by scaling axis: capacity fit R² = 0.86, layer-count fit R² = 0.49, and unified fit R² = 0.59. Experiments use DINOv2-B and the Phase 2 protocol with the backbone and decoder frozen.

fits_no_version.finding: In a frozen DINOv2-B representation autoencoder, enlarging the trainable fusion adapter from 2.5M to 113M parameters lowers ImageNet-256 rFID from 0.539 to 0.459. The authors fit this as log-linear (R²=0.86), though not monotonically (0.559 at 4.8M). Adding fused layers gives a noisy trend (linear R²=0.49), and the pooled fit has R²=0.59.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reconstruction quality of visual tokenizers improves log-linearly with the capacity of an added multi-layer feature-fusion adapter (representation-richness scaling, analogous to vocabulary scaling).

record.problems: The scaling study uses one encoder (DINOv2-B) and one visual reconstruction metric (rFID); uncertainty estimates are not reported. The layer-count and unified fits are weaker than the capacity fit, and layer-count results fluctuate. The study does not test language-model loss, training-token or compute scaling, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-sweep results were omitted. Other reported reconstruction, generation, text-to-image, and design-ablation metrics were left out because they do not measure a scaling relationship named by the tested version.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
No fixed-parameter shape comparison for language models.
No loss scaling of whole image/video models in parameters, data or compute. No repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling. Only a frozen-pipeline adapter's capacity is varied, against rFID.
Generation and GenEval are reported only for selected tokenizers, not as a function of scale.
No comparison of fitting choices or published laws.

record.verdict_notes: Single encoder, single metric, no uncertainty reported. All scaling runs are Phase 2 only (decoder frozen). layer-12 duplicates cap-3072. The GenEval overall score is 0.60 in Table 2 but 0.59 in the text. The reader's T3/V5 'tests' classification is overridden: the scaled object is an adapter, the measure is rFID, and the fitted form is log-linear over under two decades.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss is measured against parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute language-model allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count for language models.
Tests image-tokenizer reconstruction scaling with fusion capacity and layer count only. Does not test video or other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other training regimes.
Generation and text-to-image results are reported for selected tokenizers, but the study does not test whether downstream performance scales predictably with scale or pretraining loss.

The paper reports fit statistics for visual-tokenizer scaling axes, but does not test whether language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on setup or fitting choices, or whether language-model curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: DRoRAE fusion module
rows.operation_detail: Log-linear fit across expert-capacity sweep

conditions.value: fusion module only; backbone and decoder frozen

rows.measure: Log-linear fit of ImageNet-256 reconstruction rFID against fusion parameters
rows.note: The paper describes this capacity relationship as clear and reports rFID decreasing from 0.54 to 0.46 as parameters grow by ∼40×.
rows.check: Log-linear fit of rFID vs log10 adapter parameters (R²=0.86) over ~45×. Not a power law in loss for a whole model, so it cannot show V5's effect.

rows.subject: DRoRAE fusion module
rows.operation_detail: Linear fit across layer-count sweep

conditions.value: fusion module only; backbone and decoder frozen

rows.measure: Linear fit of ImageNet-256 reconstruction rFID against fused-layer count
rows.note: The trend is described as consistent improvement, but the reported fit has R² = 0.49 and the individual results fluctuate.
rows.check: This is a linear fit in layer count, not a log or power-law fit (R²=0.49). Layer count is not a V5 scale axis.

rows.subject: DRoRAE fusion module
rows.operation_detail: Unified log-linear fit across capacity- and layer-count-scaling configurations

conditions.value: expert capacity and number of fused layers
fusion module only; backbone and decoder frozen

rows.measure: Log-linear fit of ImageNet-256 reconstruction rFID against total trainable parameters
rows.note: The authors report a shared trend across both axes, but the unified fit has R² = 0.59.
rows.check: Log-linear rFID vs trainable parameters pooling both sweeps (R²=0.59); same construct mismatch as fit-capacity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Expert-capacity sweep for the DINOv2-B image tokenizer
reader_labels.reason: The reported fit has R² = 0.86, with rFID falling from 0.54 to 0.46 as fusion parameters grow by ∼40× (fit-capacity; cap-128 through cap-6144).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layer-count and unified visual-tokenizer scaling fits
reader_labels.reason: The layer-count and unified fits are weaker (R² = 0.49 and R² = 0.59), with substantial variation among layer-count results, so the evidence for a stable shared trend is limited (fit-layer-count; fit-unified; layer-1 through layer-12).
